screens.prompt: In B9, count the products whose name ends with "B".

hints.syntax: =COUNTIF(A2:A8,"*B") — the star sits before the letter to stand for everything ahead of it.
hints.func-countif: Matching part of a name is a counting question, not a lookup.
hints.require-ref: Match the pattern against the product column of the grid.
hints.value: "Widget B", "Gizmo B" and "Gadget B" end in B, so the count is 3.

docs.syntax: =COUNTIF(range, "pattern*") — * stands for any run of characters, ? for exactly one
docs.explain: Text criteria accept two wildcards, and they turn a counting question into a pattern question. The star stands for any number of characters, including none, so Widget* matches Widget A, Widget B, Widget C and Widget D but never a Gadget; the question mark stands for exactly one character, so SO-100? matches any order number one digit longer in that position. A pattern with no wildcard is an exact match, which is why COUNTIF on Widget alone answers zero rather than four: the cells hold Widget A, not Widget. Patterns are case-insensitive, so widget* and Widget* are the same test, and the whole pattern must be inside the quotes or the function sees a range and a piece of text with no comma between them. In this drill the first screen counts four names starting with Widget and the second counts two names ending in B, where the star moves in front of the letter. The usual mistake is putting the star on the wrong end, which silently counts a different set of rows rather than failing loudly.
